news.title: Claude’s new rules against game cloning won’t stop the AI copying boom
news.summary: Last week, Anthropic introduced a new system prompt designed to stop its Claude models from re-creating specific, existing video games. While that move could help shield Anthropic from some liability, it's unlikely to slow much of the massive wave of AI-assisted game porting and copying that has emerged in recent months. A social media user and AI decompilation enthusiast going by the name "chasm" was among the first to note the prompt change late last week, saying a new rule seemed to be added to the Claude Code prompt on or around October 27. That rule—included in a json file under the name "tengu_heron_brook"—reads as follows: Do build original games, games in a genre, and games from the user’s own designs and assets. Don’t build a recreation of a specific existing game, even if it is renamed or called original. XDA later independently verified that the new rule appears in version 2.1.314 of the Claude Code binary, which was released on October 30.

news.title: OpenAI pitches data center power plants as a way to protect nearby areas

As public opinion has soured on data centers, it’s selling ‘AI campuses’ as protectors, instead of noisy polluters. In an announcement on Monday, OpenAI says it will pilot its “Grid Protectors Program” at an upcoming data center in Effingham County, Georgia, where the company promises to free up to 1,000 megawatts of power during extreme weather or emergencies, enough to power air conditioners in around 700,000 homes. The announcement comes as opposition to data centers spreads across the US, in response to massive projects that have begun development and construction, frequently with little or no input from local residents. In Utah, residents protested after Box Elder County commissioners signed off on a data center expected to consume more than double the state’s peak electricity demand in 2025, and spread hot air in the desert valley surrounding the data center. Now OpenAI’s approach is to pitch the construction of power plants that feed the electricity required by the new AI data centers it’s building as “a resource that utilities can call on when communities need it most.”

news.title: The wearable on your wrist can predict blood pressure crisis events days in advance
news.summary: In the domain of wearable devices, we have reached a stage where they are available in a variety of form factors. You can go with a smartwatch, something a little more subtle like a smart band without a screen, or even a smart ring. And as the form factors have continued to evolve, so have the capabilities and the sensing hardware. What started with basic light-based heart rate tracking has now reached a stage where smartwatches are capable of tracking multiple metrics, such as taking electrocardiogram readings, tracking sleep, looking for signs of sleep apnea, or even detecting spikes in blood pressure levels. Now, fresh research courtesy of the American Heart Association claims that these mass-market wearable devices can help predict episodes of dangerously high blood pressure, or hypertensive crisis, up to three days in advance. The research was conducted over a period of 12 months and involved more than 4,000 participants living with stage 2 high blood pressure.

news.title: When You Should—and Shouldn’t—Use AI to Search the Web
news.summary: If you've interacted with the likes of Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini, you've noticed that in addition to everything else they do, these AI chatbots can search the web for you. Depending on what you’re looking for, it can be easier to find more relevant results through a chatbot, which may explain why Google is so keen to push AI Mode for its own search engine. When asked to search the web, the latest versions of these bots are combining elements of traditional web search (they're essentially just googling on your behalf) with knowledge they are able to pull out of their training data. Everything is then packaged and formatted in the now-familiar, polished generative AI style. It's the added AI elements on top of the traditional googling where the differences come in, and that means AI-powered search may not always be the best option. If you're looking up something simple and widely known—like the height of the Empire State Building—then AI search is a pretty safe bet.

news.title: Hundreds of Mundane AI Apps Are Hiding Sexually Abusive Deepfake Features
news.summary: At first glance, the self-proclaimed “pet portrait” app Viefur appears to be just another AI slop generator. Using digital coins sold in the app—around $4 will buy 130 coins—pet photos can be turned into an “anthropomorphic portrait,” with the critter dressed in “human clothing” and inserted into bizarre scenes. Think a hamster wearing beach shorts, sunglasses, and lounging in a swimming pool or a Hawaiian shirt-wearing cat, drinking from a coconut. All of this is cover for what appears to be the app’s true purpose: creating sexually abusive deepfake images. A WIRED investigation found the app is part of a network of more than 400 connected domains and apps that, like Viefur, often claim to be everyday services—such as language tuition or AI workout coaches. When accessed under certain conditions, however, apps in the network stealthily load a web interface allowing the generation of explicit AI sexual images and videos using photos users upload.

The strings were found in HomeView Software 27.2 and feature four camera modes, including Off, Detect Activity, Stream, and "Stream & Allow Recording," along with scheduling options for when users are home, away, or asleep. Notably, pdfu says there's also a HomeView-specific configuration for 1080p/30fps video and microphone input, which the software selects for HomeKit Secure Video sessions. Other strings suggest that only home members will be able to view streams and recordings. They also indicate that a green light appears and a sound plays when a stream is viewed or recording starts, and users will receive a notification when camera settings change. The scheduling options include an away mode, but the strings suggest streaming and recording can only be enabled from the HomeView itself while people are home.

news.title: AI doesn’t have to turn evil to put you at risk
news.summary: An AI assistant that agrees with everything you say might feel like the perfect companion — until you need someone to tell you you're wrong. The potential consumer benefit is straightforward: assistants that know when to push back, and that are harder to trick.

news.title: Anthropic's Claude API Adds Message Threads Beta to Cut Agent Latency by 35%
news.summary: Make long-running agents faster with message threadsNew in the Messages API, send your conversation once, and the API receives only what’s new with every turn. CategoryAnnouncementsProductClaude PlatformDateNovember 2, 2026Reading time3 minShareCopy linkMessage threads is now available in public beta on the Claude Platform. With message threads, agents no longer need to resend the full conversation history on every turn, reducing latency for long-running sessions. A coding agent might make hundreds of requests in one session, and each request resends every earlier message and tool result. Once a conversation reaches hundreds of thousands of tokens, resending all of it adds time before Claude starts responding. With message threads, agents send only what’s new since the last turn, which reduces time to first token (TTFT).

news.title: Basically no one is using AI agents for their DoorDash orders

Speaking generally, Xu said he sees the potential for AI agents to be genuinely helpful for “long consideration purchases” and major decisions where agents would be “doing work on your behalf proactively in the background.” However, Xu added, “when it comes to a task that’s as simple as ordering food, we tend to see that come directly to DoorDash.” To be fair to the AI boosters, DoorDash only rolled out its Model Context Protocol (MCP) connector less than a month ago. The connector provides a standardized, open-standard way for third-party AI tools to easily order through DoorDash’s platform. Without that kind of linkup—which is still only available to a small number of “early beta partners” and mainly used to streamline corporate lunch orders—AI agents have to go through a bit more effort to access DoorDash through a web interface, for instance.

news.title: Google Adopts IETF AIPREF Standard for Unified AI Training Controls in robots.txt
news.summary: Google also announced, like Bing, OpenAI and Anthropic, that it plans to voluntarily adopt a proposal under consideration at IETF, the global internet standard-setting body, that would create a simple, streamlined AI training control for web publishers and creators. Google said, "This will help websites express their AI training preferences across multiple AI providers in a single step and is based on work from the AIPREF working group at the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF)." This new, work-in-progress control will give websites and publishers a new way to communicate their AI training preferences across multiple AI providers. This lets them invoke their preferences in a single step in robots.txt, instead of listing each one individually. Google told me "moving forward with this initiative alongside peer AI providers as part of a shared commitment to foster an open, creator-first web ecosystem, and following feedback from publishers, civil society and regulators calling for an easier way for websites to express their AI training preferences." news.title: Pope Leo XIV Urges UN to Ban Lethal Autonomous Weapons, Calls AI "Tools, Not Persons
news.summary: UN member states should take steps to ban ‘lethal autonomous weapons,’ Pope Leo says. UN member states should take steps to ban ‘lethal autonomous weapons,’ Pope Leo says. Pope Leo XIV says AI systems should be “disarmed,” adding that humans “have the responsibility to guide, change and, when necessary, reject its applications.” In Friday’s Papal Address, Pope Leo encourages United Nations member states to “take concrete steps toward banning lethal autonomous weapons” during their meeting in Geneva next month. The address reflects many of the ideas Pope Leo laid out in his first major papal document in May, which highlighted “safeguarding the human person in the time of artificial intelligence.” In line with his encyclical, Pope Leo tells participants that “Machines are tools, not persons,” and warns about the dangers of granting AI systems rights or legal personhood. “Decisions affecting human life, freedom, and the use of force must always remain subject to effective, informed, and responsible human oversight,” Pope Leo says. In 2024, Pope Francis similarly called for a ban on autonomous weapons, saying, “No machine should ever choose to take the life of a human being.” AI has become a popular topic for Pope Leo, who suggests he chose his name because he must confront advances in the technology — similar to how Pope Leo XIII presided over the church at the forefront of the Industrial Revolution.

news.title: A Defense Contractor Gave Their Personal AI Agent Access to a Secure Pentagon System
news.summary: Earlier this year, sources tell WIRED, a contractor caused a security incident at the Department of Defense by connecting a secure centralized system used by multiple intelligence agencies to their personal account for Claude Code, Anthropic’s AI coding agent. It appears that the agent used by the contractor, who is employed by the global consulting firm Accenture, then sent information about the DOD system, including login credentials, to a high-risk, third-party website. The centralized system contains controlled unclassified information (CUI), which is considered sensitive and not to be released to the public without review. CUI can include information about critical infrastructure, nuclear submarine propulsion, and vulnerabilities to chemical and biological terrorism. Additionally, security experts say, access to the system could allow for the exploitation of even more sensitive ones. “It puts all the data that’s in there at risk,” says a source aware of the incident, who requested anonymity as they were not authorized to speak to the press.

news.summary: (opens in a new window)Loading…ShareOrganizing the Spec around core valuesOrganizing the Spec around core valuesNew and retired sectionsWhat comes nextOrganizing the Spec around core valuesNew and retired sectionsWhat comes nextAs OpenAI's models get smarter and take more consequential actions in the world, it becomes increasingly important that they go beyond just interpreting the specific instructions they receive. Models also need to understand human intentions and values, so they can exercise good judgment in situations their instructions don’t explicitly address while remaining faithful to human intent and oversight. Today OpenAI is updating the Model Spec⁠(opens in a new window), OpenAI's public description of how OpenAI want OpenAI's models to behave. The update reorganizes its guidance around five underlying values: faithfulness to human intent, harm minimization, honesty and transparency, human agency, and care. This reflects an aim of OpenAI's work on value alignment: for models to understand and apply human values in unfamiliar situations, while remaining faithful to human intent. Alongside clearer explanations of existing principles, the revision adds guidance on context, oversight, and agency, adjusts some behavioral defaults, and retires much of the detailed style guidance.

news.title: The ‘Pain in the Ass’ Math That Could Save Vibe Coding From Itself
news.summary: Stanford researcher Chuyue Sun and her fellow computer scientists developed an AI tool that completed an engineering project in less than half a day for under $500, compared to the five months it took three highly skilled experts to do the same work manually. The dramatic reduction in time and cost, which Sun reported in a recent paper, is among the early results that are awakening an obscure field of coding and mathematics known as formal verification. For decades, developers have envisioned using math to prove that their software is bug-free. This process is long and laborious, requiring engineers to write precise statements about the goals of their software and convert their code into formulas that can be validated. While companies already run sophisticated tests to identify as many flaws in their software as possible, they rarely shell out for formal verification, which can catch even more erratic behavior. Now, a wave of startups is betting that generative AI will make formal software verification both practical and essential.

news.title: OpenAI Updates Model Spec With 5 Core Values to Guide More Capable AI Systems
news.summary: (opens in a new window)Loading…ShareOrganizing the Spec around core valuesOrganizing the Spec around core valuesNew and retired sectionsWhat comes nextOrganizing the Spec around core valuesNew and retired sectionsWhat comes nextAs our models get smarter and take more consequential actions in the world, it becomes increasingly important that they go beyond just interpreting the specific instructions they receive. Models also need to understand human intentions and values, so they can exercise good judgment in situations their instructions don’t explicitly address while remaining faithful to human intent and oversight. Today we’re updating the Model Spec⁠(opens in a new window), our public description of how we want our models to behave. The update reorganizes its guidance around five underlying values: faithfulness to human intent, harm minimization, honesty and transparency, human agency, and care. This reflects an aim of our work on value alignment: for models to understand and apply human values in unfamiliar situations, while remaining faithful to human intent. Alongside clearer explanations of existing principles, the revision adds guidance on context, oversight, and agency, adjusts some behavioral defaults, and retires much of the detailed style guidance.

news.title: Gemini App Now Lets Users Generate, Edit & Preview Docs, PDFs & Spreadsheets In-Chat
news.summary: We’re introducing new ways to create and refine documents, PDFs, presentations, spreadsheets, code, and more in the Gemini app. You can now generate, preview, and edit files right within your chat — expand to full screen to type edits directly, highlight text to ask questions, or have Gemini refine your files. PDF preview and editing is supported on both the web and mobile, while all other formats (Google Docs, Google Sheets, slide decks, Markdown files, TXT files, and code) are supported on the web only. As shown in the video below, you can now ask Gemini to create a PDF study guide from your uploaded handwritten lecture notes and then you can easily manually edit, highlight specific sections to have Gemini make edits to text or visuals, and even ask further questions. These capabilities are now available to all users in all languages where Gemini app is available.

news.title: Mistral Large 4 tops open models outside China with 63% cost cut and stronger coding
news.summary: Mistral has released open weights for its trillion-parameter Large 4 model, nicknamed Le Chonk, under a custom license. Independent evaluator Artificial Analysis scores it 26 points on Intelligence Index v5, making it the top open-weight model developed outside China, though it trails DeepSeek and GLM-5.3 globally. Cost per task dropped 63% from $5.54 to $2.06. On the Coding Agent Index, ML4 ranks second among open-weight models, using 47% fewer tokens than leader GLM-5.3. The license requires a separate commercial agreement for model-as-a-service operators.

news.title: Gemini Notebook Adds Hundreds of Free Textbooks from OpenStax & S Chand for Students
news.summary: Last month, we introduced Expert Intelligence, a cross-Google initiative that helps you engage with your trusted sources through Google AI products. While you can already add eligible ebooks purchased from Google Play Books, today we’re expanding that experience so students can easily add materials for their courses. Students can now access hundreds of textbooks from providers in the U.S. and India including OpenStax, Open Textbook Library, and S Chand Publishing, right in Gemini Notebook at no charge. Once you add a textbook, every answer is grounded directly in the textbook, with inline citations and direct links back to the original source. Gemini Notebook also lets you transform textbook content into tailored study guides, practice quizzes, flashcards, and more.

news.title: ElevenLabs Launches SFX v3 Sound Effects Generator with Text Prompt Control
news.summary: ElevenLabs has launched SFX v3, a new sound effects generator integrated into its ElevenCreative platform. The tool allows users to create original sound effects from text prompts, offering greater control over the detail, context, and character of each generation. Described as enabling richer and more precise sound design, SFX v3 lets creators describe exactly what they need, whether specific ambient sounds, sharp mechanical effects, or complex audio environments, making professional sound design more accessible through natural language input.
